question: Can the soliton crystal read its own past through a physical delay line, a chain of rotors of its own kind that carries both the delay and the stored phase and whose heat is counted, and is the crystal with its line a cheaper clock than the crystal alone?
seeds: seed(name) = int(sha256('<registration id>:<beacon randomness>:<name>').hexdigest()[:12], 16): the crystal's noise from the cell name, the line's from '<cell name>:line'; numpy PCG64.
beacon: drand quicknet (chain 52db9ba70e0cc0f6eaf7803dd07447a1f5477735fd3f661792ba94600c84e971): the first round dated at or after the earliest GitHub-witnessed push (GET repos/s0fractal/time-lab/activity) that holds the commit adding q4-line/registration.lock.json.

design.feedback: F(t) = F − k (Φ(t) − ψ_L(t) − Λ*), clipped to [0, 2F]; stage i of the line: n_s ψ_i'' = n_s K sin(ψ_{i−1} − ψ_i) − γ n_s ψ_i' + noise at σ², ψ_0 = Φ, one-way pull; Λ* the line's mean lag at k = 0 (calibration; 32 interpolated). ideal: F(t) = F − k (Φ(t) − Φ(t − τ) − v* τ) from a free exact buffer.

hypotheses.statement: A physical line can stand in for a free exact buffer: through a line of 16-phase stages the crystal gains the same as through a perfect delay line of the line's delay (16.5), within a factor of two.
hypotheses.rule: For each cell, of the crystal's mean phase Φ = J / (N d) at the checkpoints (400, 800, 1800), 1024 trajectories: D = [var(Φ(t2) − Φ(t0)) − var(Φ(t1) − Φ(t0))] / (2 (t2 − t1)), v = mean(Φ(t2) − Φ(t0)) / (t2 − t0), S = the mean heat given to the bath by the crystal and the line over [t0, t2] / (σ² (t2 − t0)), η = v² / (D S); the gain G = D(alone) / D(cell). Each test is log10 of a ratio of gains or of η, with a 95% interval (inverted-cdf quantiles) over 2000 resamples of every cell's trajectories, seeded from the registration id; a resample with a non-positive D counts that side as infinitely precise, one with both non-positive is undefined, and any undefined resample makes the hypothesis inconclusive. Supported if the interval of log10 G(line-n16) / G(ideal) lies inside (−log10 2, log10 2); contradicted if it lies wholly above log10 2 or wholly below −log10 2; else inconclusive.

hypotheses.statement: The crystal with a line of 8-phase stages is a cheaper clock than the crystal alone: its precision per entropy, the line's heat counted, is higher.
hypotheses.rule: For each cell, of the crystal's mean phase Φ = J / (N d) at the checkpoints (400, 800, 1800), 1024 trajectories: D = [var(Φ(t2) − Φ(t0)) − var(Φ(t1) − Φ(t0))] / (2 (t2 − t1)), v = mean(Φ(t2) − Φ(t0)) / (t2 − t0), S = the mean heat given to the bath by the crystal and the line over [t0, t2] / (σ² (t2 − t0)), η = v² / (D S); the gain G = D(alone) / D(cell). Each test is log10 of a ratio of gains or of η, with a 95% interval (inverted-cdf quantiles) over 2000 resamples of every cell's trajectories, seeded from the registration id; a resample with a non-positive D counts that side as infinitely precise, one with both non-positive is undefined, and any undefined resample makes the hypothesis inconclusive. Supported if the interval of log10 η(line-n8) / η(alone) lies above 0; contradicted if it lies wholly below 0; else inconclusive.

hypotheses.statement: A line too light to hold its values ruins the clock: through a line of 4-phase stages, whose stages slip, the crystal diffuses at least twice as much as alone.
hypotheses.rule: For each cell, of the crystal's mean phase Φ = J / (N d) at the checkpoints (400, 800, 1800), 1024 trajectories: D = [var(Φ(t2) − Φ(t0)) − var(Φ(t1) − Φ(t0))] / (2 (t2 − t1)), v = mean(Φ(t2) − Φ(t0)) / (t2 − t0), S = the mean heat given to the bath by the crystal and the line over [t0, t2] / (σ² (t2 − t0)), η = v² / (D S); the gain G = D(alone) / D(cell). Each test is log10 of a ratio of gains or of η, with a 95% interval (inverted-cdf quantiles) over 2000 resamples of every cell's trajectories, seeded from the registration id; a resample with a non-positive D counts that side as infinitely precise, one with both non-positive is undefined, and any undefined resample makes the hypothesis inconclusive. Supported if the interval of log10 G(line-n4) lies below −log10 2; contradicted if it lies wholly above −log10 2; else inconclusive.

hypotheses.statement: Paying for a heavier line stops paying: the crystal with 8-phase stages is at least 1.5 times as efficient a clock as with 32-phase stages.
hypotheses.rule: For each cell, of the crystal's mean phase Φ = J / (N d) at the checkpoints (400, 800, 1800), 1024 trajectories: D = [var(Φ(t2) − Φ(t0)) − var(Φ(t1) − Φ(t0))] / (2 (t2 − t1)), v = mean(Φ(t2) − Φ(t0)) / (t2 − t0), S = the mean heat given to the bath by the crystal and the line over [t0, t2] / (σ² (t2 − t0)), η = v² / (D S); the gain G = D(alone) / D(cell). Each test is log10 of a ratio of gains or of η, with a 95% interval (inverted-cdf quantiles) over 2000 resamples of every cell's trajectories, seeded from the registration id; a resample with a non-positive D counts that side as infinitely precise, one with both non-positive is undefined, and any undefined resample makes the hypothesis inconclusive. Supported if the interval of log10 η(line-n8) / η(line-n32) lies above log10 1.5; contradicted if it lies wholly below log10 1.5; else inconclusive.
